original_question: If u and v are independent unitaries in the ultrapower NU, determine whether they can be lifted to sequences of pairwise independent unitaries in N.
target_in_paper: Problem 29 in the section "Lifting problems": the open question about lifting independent unitaries from an ultrapower to representatives in the ground algebra with coordinatewise pairwise independence. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2511.20377v1))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right part of the paper: it is about independent unitaries living in an ultrapower N^\mathcal U, and it asks whether one can choose lifts back in N with an independence property at each coordinate. Those are the core ingredients of Problem 29. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2511.20377v1))
missing_details: The paper-wide notation first fixes a nonprincipal ultrafilter \mathcal U on \mathbb N and writes N^\mathcal U for the tracial ultrapower of a tracial von Neumann algebra N. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2511.20377v1))
Immediately before Problem 29, the paper defines n-independence and says that plain "independent" means ∞-independent. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2511.20377v1))
The definition of independence is by traces of alternating centered words in the given unitaries; without that, the draft is not stand-alone. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2511.20377v1))
The official formulation is an open problem, not a statement already known to be true or false in general. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2511.20377v1))

The lifting should be spelled out as choosing representing sequences of unitaries in N whose classes in N^\mathcal U are the prescribed ultrapower unitaries. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2511.20377v1))
The paper's wording is plural and does not single out a named pair u,v; your draft hard-codes a two-unitary special case. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2511.20377v1))

The target property is coordinatewise: for each index m, the chosen representatives in N should be pairwise independent, not merely asymptotically independent modulo \mathcal U. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2511.20377v1))
To stay paper-faithful, one should not switch to the nearby Problem 30, which is the distinct n-independent variant. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2511.20377v1))
refined_question: Let N be a tracial von Neumann algebra and \mathcal U a nonprincipal ultrafilter on \mathbb N. Suppose one is given independent unitaries in U(N^\mathcal U), where "independent" means ∞-independent in the sense that every alternating centered word in them has trace 0. Can one choose representing sequences of unitaries in N for these ultrapower elements so that, for every index m, the chosen representatives are pairwise independent unitaries in N? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2511.20377v1))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation because Section "Lifting problems" contains a uniquely matching problem: Problem 29 asks exactly about lifting independent unitaries from an ultrapower, and the immediately preceding definition supplies the intended meaning of "independent." The next item, Problem 30, is the separate n-independent version, so broadening or shifting to that nearby problem would not be faithful. The note after Problem 29 also confirms that only special cases are known. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2511.20377v1))
